extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers / the American public
extracted.subtask_description: A multi-item newspaper page (wire copy and opinion) reporting World War II events, casualties, foreign reactions, and commentary on press freedom and post-war objectives. Includes news dispatches, human-interest items, and a policy-oriented statement about government control of news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of the press / free of government control
rubrics_metrics.description: “God save the United States from a centralized government dominated source of news, especially of Government activities. Already the International Food Conference in Virginia and the Refugee Conference in the Bermudas are following the dangerous pattern of a Government-control of news in non-military activities.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument that government-controlled foreign news agencies and centralized government control of news keep the truth from the people and permit stirring of rancor, race and economic hatreds that can lead to war; implication that news organizations/coverage should resist government domination and maintain independence. Examples cited: International Food Conference (Virginia) and Refugee Conference (Bermudas) as following this dangerous pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding propaganda / government-controlled foreign news agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: “Kent Cooper points out the dire effects of constant propaganda by Government-controlled foreign news agencies. That policy kept the truth from the people and permitted the stirring of rancor, race and economic hatreds which led directly to the present war.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial/policy criterion: news coverage and foreign news agencies should not be instruments of government propaganda; independent reporting is necessary to prevent misinformation and social division. Used here as a rationale for opposing government control of news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and public scrutiny of international decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: “The consequence is that decisions of a non-military meeting... will be imparted to us without any opportunity for a thoroughgoing scrutiny by the people of what is being done... to accept secret covenants secretly arrived at is to permit a handful of men and women to make decisions affecting the lives and futures of more than 2,000,000,000 without affording to these any opportunity to judge the wisdom and ... of what was done.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative standard: international conferences (especially non-military/post-war planning) should be open to public scrutiny and debate rather than decided by secret agreements; implies journalists and news organizations should demand and provide transparent coverage, and policymakers should include representative input (e.g., Congressional representation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible/limited censorship in wartime contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: “The patriotic citizens of America do not question responsible censorship by the United Nations.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes acceptable, responsible censorship (presumably for military/security reasons) from unacceptable government control or secrecy; establishes a boundary for when censorship may be tolerable versus when free press principles should prevail.
